overview: This one-page joint State Department–Economic Cooperation Administration despatch from the American Embassy in Seoul reports the planned July 1949 visit of ECA postal consultant G. N. Miller and two Korean postal officials to Tokyo. The delegation was to negotiate postwar postal relations between South Korea and Japan, including parcel-post arrangements, international rates and charges, mail statistics, sea and air carriage contracts, prohibited matter, and exchanges of newspapers and periodicals; any resulting agreements would require approval by the South Korean government.

subfiles.title: Despatch on G. N. Miller’s postal mission to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports the objectives and planned participants of a Korean postal delegation’s July 1949 visit to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy reports that ECA postal consultant G. N. Miller would visit Tokyo with the chief of Korea’s Postal Bureau and a Korean international-mails section chief during the week of July 11. Their agenda included establishing parcel-post relations, calculating rates and handling charges from May 1949 statistics, arranging Japanese steamship and air carriage contracts, reviewing mail prohibitions with SCAP officials, and discussing newspaper and periodical exchanges. Miller was authorized to negotiate for the Republic of Korea, but all agreements remained subject to Korean government approval. The despatch was issued jointly by the State Department and ECA.

interest: The despatch provides a compact view of the practical reconstruction of communications between South Korea and Japan in the early postwar occupation period. It is especially useful for showing how postal normalization involved not only bilateral officials but also the ECA, SCAP, private Japanese carriers, empirical traffic data, and South Korean governmental approval. Its detailed agenda illuminates the administrative infrastructure underlying renewed regional relations before the formal normalization of Japan–South Korea diplomatic ties.
